root_cause.what: TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str' at score_c1_confirmation.score_battery line 104, `spec["n"]`
root_cause.why: both D-series scorers built their set mapping as {name: f"{name}.jsonl"} -- name to FILENAME -- while the shared score_battery reads spec["n"] and spec["domain"] out of each value. It derives the file path from the KEY, so the filename value was never read for anything.
root_cause.both_scorers: score_d1_screening.py AND score_d1_confirmation.py carried the identical defect, so repairing screening alone would have hit the same wall at the confirmation rung.
root_cause.why_nothing_caught_it: every test exercised battery_sets or score_battery, never the two together, and the scorers only ever execute as a pod subprocess.

repair.fix: both scorers now build specs from battery_family.strata(), which owns the counts: {name: {"n": n, "domain": domain}}. Nothing invents an expected item count.
repair.regression: scripts/stages/stage-1/phase_d1/tests/test_d1_scorer_set_specs.py -- 12 tests running the REAL score_battery over the REAL 950-item battery with the REAL battery_sets() output, plus a mutation feeding the old filename shape and requiring TypeError.
repair.downstream_verified_at_zero: the whole post-scoring path to ALL_DONE: the real scorer CLI produces every one of the five keys the driver reads (correct_overall, usable_rollout_rate, n, n_scorable, result_sha256), the ranking rows carry the four fields rank_screening reads, and rank_screening/advance_one were already covered.
